SIE EXAM STUDY GUIDE

How to use SIE practice questions without memorizing the answer key

SIE practice questions work best when each wrong answer changes what you do next. Identify the tested rule, read why your choice fails, and then return to that topic in a later mixed set. Repeating a familiar question until you recognize it is much less useful than explaining the rule in a new scenario.

Reviewed 2026-09-07. Based on FINRA's published SIE format and content outline.

Read the whole fact pattern first

Many SIE questions turn on a word such as primary, secondary, discretionary, or prohibited. Before scanning choices, ask what the question is actually testing. This makes distractors easier to eliminate and builds the habit needed when the wording changes on the real exam.

Treat an explanation as a short lesson

When you miss, do not stop at the correct letter. Find the rule that makes it correct and the assumption that made your selection wrong. Bona Fide shows a rationale for the choice you selected, so the feedback addresses the exact confusion rather than a generic answer key.

Put this into practice

Bona Fide turns a study date and recent answers into a visible next set. Download it on the App Store.

Download on the App Store

Mix old and weak topics

Topic drills are good for learning a new concept. Mixed sets are better for deciding which rule applies without a hint. Alternate both modes: drill a weak domain, then test it among unrelated questions a day or two later.

Keep the official outline nearby

FINRA's content outline is the authoritative source for what can be tested. Use this guide to organize your study, then check the original whenever you need the exact wording or current exam information.
